venue.name: Comox Archives and Museum
venue.description: The Comox Archives and Museum is a non-profit community museum and archives at 1729 Comox Avenue in Comox. Its displays cover the early development and history of the region, and there is a temporary exhibit area for current community research and engagement. The site also describes a family history library and archival holdings that can be seen by appointment. It is open Tuesday to Saturday.

programs.name: Group visit
programs.description: The museum is open to the public Tuesday to Saturday and its displays cover the early development and history of the region, with a temporary exhibit area alongside. The current display is about life in Comox in 1945 and 1946. The site does not describe school or daycare programs, a group rate, a booking route for groups or how far ahead to ask, so a group visit has to be arranged by phone. One of their own news posts describes a group of children coming in for a museum art tour, so children's groups have been hosted before even though nothing is advertised.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the museum rooms and look at wall panels of photographs, documents and objects about the early history of Comox, plus whatever is in the temporary exhibit area at the time.
programs.our_note: This is a small local museum in one building, so plan a short stop rather than a whole morning. Nothing about group bookings, prices or the youngest age they take is anywhere on their site, so phone first and ask what they can set up for you.
programs.practical_summary: Nothing is published about toilets, somewhere to eat lunch, or parking for a bus, and the museum never says what it charges. One phone call would settle all of it before you commit.
programs.extra_fees_note: The site asks for donations to support the society's ongoing work but never states an admission price, a group rate or whether entry is free.
programs.evidence: The museum displays showcase the early development and history of the region.

images.alt: An indoor museum gallery with a wood floor, display panels of framed photographs and documents along both walls, and two chairs beside a small draped table.
A museum room with a wood floor and track lighting, wall panels of framed historical photographs, a display case, a wooden chair, and a sign reading Archives.

gaps: no school or daycare programs published anywhere on the site; the museum never mentions hosting groups, so whether it takes them is unknown rather than refused
no admission price, group rate or statement that entry is free; the site only invites donations to the society, so cost is unknown
no capacity, no lead time or notice period for a booking, and no stated booking route for groups
no washrooms, lunch space, rain backup, stroller access, wheelchair access or bus parking information anywhere on the site
no duration published for a visit
months unknown; the site gives weekdays but never says whether the museum closes for part of the year
the archives are a research service rather than a children's activity: material is viewed by appointment, arranged by phone
no map embed, no coordinates and no structured address markup on the site, so the point was derived from the published street address
alt text for both images was written by us after opening the image files in a browser and looking at them; the site's own alt attributes are empty
the site publishes no Open Graph image and no exterior photograph of the building, so the hero is an interior gallery view from the home page
a July 2023 news post describes children from a summer art camp visiting for a museum art tour, but no art tour is offered or priced anywhere else on the site

conflicts.note: Their own pages give two different opening times. One says 10am to 4pm, another says 12pm to 4pm, both Tuesday to Saturday. Worth checking when you book, especially if you want a morning.
Two different email addresses appear on their site. If one bounces, try the other. We use the one from their contact page.
Their contact page and their archives page give phone numbers that differ by one digit. If one does not connect, try the other. We use the contact page number.
